name: Kolya and Movie Theatre
description: Recently, Kolya found out that a new movie theatre is going to be opened in his city soon, which will show a new movie every day for $$$n$$$ days. So, on the day with the number $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, the movie theatre will show the premiere of the $$$i$$$-th movie. Also, Kolya found out the schedule of the movies and assigned the entertainment value to each movie, denoted by $$$a_i$$$. However, the longer Kolya stays without visiting a movie theatre, the larger the decrease in entertainment value of the next movie. That decrease is equivalent to $$$d \cdot cnt$$$, where $$$d$$$ is a predetermined value and $$$cnt$$$ is the number of days since the last visit to the movie theatre. It is also known that Kolya managed to visit another movie theatre a day before the new one opened — the day with the number $$$0$$$. So if we visit the movie theatre the first time on the day with the number $$$i$$$, then $$$cnt$$$ — the number of days since the last visit to the movie theatre will be equal to $$$i$$$ . For example, if $$$d = 2$$$ and $$$a = [3, 2, 5, 4, 6]$$$, then by visiting movies with indices $$$1$$$ and $$$3$$$, $$$cnt$$$ value for the day $$$1$$$ will be equal to $$$1 - 0 = 1$$$ and $$$cnt$$$ value for the day $$$3$$$ will be $$$3 - 1 = 2$$$, so the total entertainment value of the movies will be $$$a_1 - d \cdot 1 + a_3 - d \cdot 2 = 3 - 2 \cdot 1 + 5 - 2 \cdot 2 = 2$$$. Unfortunately, Kolya only has time to visit at most $$$m$$$ movies . Help him create a plan to visit the cinema in such a way that the total entertainment value of all the movies he visits is maximized.
input_specification: Each test consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and $$$d$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le m \le n$$$, $$$1 \le d \le 10^9$$$). The second line of each set of input data contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$-10^9 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the entertainment values of the movies. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the maximum total entertainment value that Kolya can get.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1862E — Kolya and Movie Theatre [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
